title: cinnamon rolls
description: with maple frosting and roasted pecans
tags: cinnamon rolls, breakfast, baking, nuts, bread, sweet

directions.step: In a glass measuring cup add the warm water, 2t of the sugar, and the yeast. Let stand for 5 minutes until it forms bubbles.
Add the eggs, melted butter, salt, mashed potatoes, remaining 2/3C sugar, and bread flour to a large bowl. Add the yeast mixture slowly and mix until well blended. Knead for 5 minutes.

directions: Cover the dough and let rise until doubled, about 2 hours.

directions.step: Punch down the dough and roll out into a long rectangle, long enough to yield twelve 1.5" slices. Spread with the melted butter, then sprinkle evenly with the brown sugar, cinnamon, and roasted chopped pecans to cover.

directions: Roll the dough up lengthwise into a tight log and cut into twelve 1.5" slices.
Grease a 9x13 baking dish and arrange the 12 slices in it. Let rise again until doubled in size.
Bake at 350°F for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown. Let cool completely before icing.

directions.step: Once the rolls are cool, make the icing. In a medium saucepan melt the butter over high heat until it just starts to boil. Add the brown sugar.

directions: Bring to a boil, then lower heat to medium and continue to boil for exactly 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Do not boil longer than 2 minutes.

directions.step: Add the milk and maple extract and return to a boil, stirring constantly. As soon as it begins to boil, remove from heat and cool to lukewarm.
Gradually add the sifted confectioners' sugar, stirring with a wooden spoon until thick and spreadable. Spread over the cooled rolls.
Sprinkle roasted chopped pecans over the icing.

notes: DRAFT: pecan amounts are TBD — both in the filling and on top of the icing.
Makes 12 rolls baked in a 9x13 dish. Roll the dough long enough to cut twelve 1.5" slices.
Original recipe makes fewer rolls in an 8" cake pan; this is the scaled-up 12-roll version.
